card.title: THE SILENT SEVENTH
card.text: Once per turn, draw a card when you play your left-most card. Becomes Veteran after the third time.
card.flavorText: The 7th Australian Division was an infantry formation of the Second Australian Imperial Force during WWII. It became known as the Silent Seventh because many felt its achievements received less attention than those of other Australian divisions. One reason was wartime censorship around its hard fighting in the Syria-Lebanon campaign of 1941. The division was one of the few Australian formations to serve in both the Middle East and the South West Pacific theaters. In the Middle East, the 7th Division fought at Giarabub, Tobruk, and in Syria and Lebanon, where it advanced through difficult terrain toward Beirut. After Japan entered the war, the division was recalled to defend Australia. Elements were lost in Java, but most of the division returned home, before being sent to New Guinea. In Papua, the division fought on the Kokoda Track, at Milne Bay, Buna Gona, and later in the Markham and Ramu valleys. It helped capture Lae and fought through the Finisterre Range, at the Battle of Shaggy Ridge in particular. In 1945, the division took part in its final campaign at Balikpapan in Borneo, before disbanding in 1946.
